prompt: Some people believe that the widespread use of computers and mobile phones has weakened young people's reading and writing skills. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Some people argue that the widespread use of computers and mobile phones has weakened young people's reading and writing abilities. I completely disagree with this view because digital technology provides access to a wider range of reading materials and creates numerous opportunities for young people to practise written communication.

I completely disagree with the claim that computers and mobile phones have weakened young people's reading abilities. In fact, digital technology has provided access to a much wider range of reading materials than was previously available. Students can now read e-books, online newspapers, academic articles and educational websites whenever they need them. For example, a university student can use a smartphone to read research papers and international news while travelling or waiting for a class. Because these materials are readily available, young people can develop a regular reading habit without depending entirely on printed books. As a result, technology can contribute to stronger vocabulary and reading comprehension.

Computers and mobile phones can also support the development of writing skills because they give young people frequent opportunities to communicate through written language. Although texting is usually informal, students also write emails, prepare assignments, participate in online discussions and communicate with teachers through digital platforms. For instance, a student who regularly prepares presentations and submits written assignments online has to organise ideas clearly and use appropriate vocabulary. This repeated practice can improve written communication, particularly when young people receive feedback and correct their mistakes. Therefore, widespread technology use does not necessarily weaken writing skills; when used appropriately, it can strengthen them.

In conclusion, I completely disagree that computers and mobile phones have weakened young people's reading and writing abilities. They provide access to extensive reading materials and create numerous opportunities for written communication.
